It details Board members' unrestricted access to company information, continuous information flow, advance distribution of agendas, and director input. It lists five Board meetings held in fiscal 2025, director attendance percentages, and AGM attendance. It describes governance of Board committees, including member appointment, meeting frequency, quorum, and committee recommendations. It lists eight Board committees and their members. Finally, it details the Audit Committee's composition, objectives, charter, and processes to fulfill its objectives.

nodes.title: Audit Committee
nodes.summary: The corporate governance report details the Audit Committee's composition with four independent directors, objectives, and charter compliance with Indian and US regulations. It outlines processes for fulfilling objectives, including internal audit oversight and auditor meetings. Governance details cover membership, qualifications, and seven meetings held with full attendance. Key activities include reviewing financial statements, internal controls, risk management, auditor performance, related party transactions, and compliance. Recommendations to the Board encompass acceptance of financial statements, auditor appointments, and policy reviews. The Committee concludes that financial statements are fairly presented and internal controls are effective, with all Board recommendations accepted.

nodes.title: Nomination and Remuneration Committee
nodes.summary: The text details the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, including its composition of four independent directors (D. Sundaram as Chairperson, Michael Gibbs, Govind Iyer, Nitin Paranjpe) as of March 31, 2025. It outlines the committee's objectives, such as assisting the Board with remuneration, succession planning, director qualifications, equity plan administration, board diversity, and corporate governance policies. It notes compliance with the Committee Charter, Section 178 of the Companies Act 2013, Regulation 19 of Listing Regulations, and NYSE guidelines. Meeting frequency (four times in fiscal 2025) and full attendance are reported, along with key activities: recommending Egon Zehnder for board evaluation, reviewing succession plans, amending policies, granting stock incentives, annual self-evaluation, and revising senior management compensation. The charter and policy URLs are provided.

nodes.title: Corporate Social Responsibility Committee
nodes.summary: The text details the Corporate Social Responsibility Committee, including its composition of three independent directors (Govind Iyer, Chitra Nayak, Michael Gibbs), chaired by Govind Iyer. It outlines the CSR philosophy, objectives and responsibilities, governance, and compliance with Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013. It covers committee meetings (four in fiscal 2025) with full attendance, policy and charter adoption, and the CSR report. Financial details include expenditure of ₹523.70 crore in India, unspent balance of ₹16.15 crore, and ₹46.26 crore on ongoing projects, plus ₹40 crore spent outside India. It also lists the committee's roles in identifying CSR activities, recommending expenditure, evaluating proposals, implementing policy, formulating action plans, reviewing initiatives, coordinating with foundations, reviewing impact assessments and disclosures, and overseeing activities.

nodes.title: ESG Committee
nodes.summary: The text details Infosys' ESG Committee and Risk Management Committee. For the ESG Committee, it covers its constitution in 2021, independent director composition, objectives including guiding ESG vision, reviewing operations council, ensuring sustainability reporting compliance, and reviewing charter. It lists members, meeting frequency (four times in fiscal 2025), attendance details, key activities like reporting to the board, reviewing ESG progress and climate actions, and includes links to charter and reports. For the Risk Management Committee, it outlines its independent director composition, objectives such as overseeing risk identification and mitigation, monitoring enterprise risk management, reviewing cybersecurity risks, and coordinating with the Audit Committee. It notes committee governance, charter link, meeting frequency, and composition and attendance details.

nodes.title: Risk Management Committee
nodes.summary: The text covers the Risk Management Committee and its Cybersecurity Risk Sub-committee for Infosys in fiscal 2025. It details committee composition (all independent directors), including chairpersons D. Sundaram and Michael Gibbs, and lists members. It outlines the Risk Management Committee's ten objectives, including risk oversight, ERM framework approval, risk assessment, cybersecurity risk evaluation, Audit Committee coordination, charter review, and Chief Risk Officer appointment. Governance compliance with charter, Regulation 21, and NYSE guidelines is noted. Meeting attendance for four meetings is provided, along with key activities: reviewing macroeconomic, geopolitical, reputation, competitive, gen AI, currency, regulatory, service delivery, client credit, ESG, and cybersecurity risks; policy reviews; Board reporting; and annual self-evaluation. The Cybersecurity Sub-committee's purpose, formation, meetings, and attendance are also summarized.

nodes.title: Cybersecurity Risk Sub-committee
nodes.summary: The text covers the Cybersecurity Risk Sub-committee, comprising four independent directors: Michael Gibbs (Chairperson and cybersecurity expert), D. Sundaram, Govind Iyer, and Chitra Nayak. It details the committee's governance, including its voluntary formation in April 2019 to assess cybersecurity risks and preparedness, and its reporting to the Risk Management Committee. It notes four meetings held in fiscal 2025 with 100% attendance, provides meeting dates and attendance details, and lists key activities: reviewing security awareness initiatives, tech stack modernization, cloud security, AI and quantum computing, external threat landscape, vulnerability management, incident metrics, ransomware preparedness, and cybersecurity incidents with mitigation progress. Signed by Michael Gibbs on April 9, 2025.

nodes.title: Stakeholders Relationship Committee
nodes.summary: The Stakeholders Relationship Committee section of the Infosys Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers the committee's composition, with four independent directors and Michael Gibbs as Chairperson, and the appointment of A.G.S. Manikantha as Compliance Officer and Nodal Officer for IEPF compliance. It outlines the committee's purpose, objectives, and responsibilities, including resolving security holders' concerns, monitoring investor service standards, understanding shareholder views, and overseeing engagement and communication plans. The committee's governance framework is described, referencing Section 178 of the Companies Act, 2013, Regulation 20 of the Listing Regulations, NYSE guidelines, and the Committee Charter. Meeting attendance details show 100% attendance across four meetings held on specific dates, with all members present via video call. Complaints data for 2024 and 2025 is provided, showing received and resolved numbers. Key activities include monitoring stakeholder grievances, reviewing measures for unclaimed dividends, reviewing IEPF transfers, reviewing RTA audit reports, reviewing voting rights measures, reviewing service standards, conducting self-evaluation, reviewing investor interactions, and recommending amendments to policies and the Charter. The report is signed by Michael Gibbs.

nodes.title: Fairness and excellence
nodes.summary: The text covers Infosys' corporate governance, focusing on fairness and excellence through Board evaluation and compensation. It details the annual Board evaluation process conducted by Egon Zehnder, including independent director roles and performance indicators. It explains executive compensation tied to long-term performance, the Chairman's voluntary non-remuneration, and independent directors' compensation capped at 1% of net profit, with a breakdown of fees and total remuneration. It also covers indemnification agreements, confirmation of no binding agreements or materially significant related party transactions, employment agreements with the executive director, auditor fees, senior management particulars including changes, and compliance with regulations regarding compensation agreements.

nodes.title: Integrity and transparency & Relationship with stakeholders
nodes.summary: This corporate governance report covers Infosys's integrity and stakeholder transparency principles, corporate history from 1981 incorporation through name changes, IPOs, NASDAQ/NYSE listings, and delistings, plus bonus issues and stock splits increasing shares from 1 to 16,384. It details fiscal 2025 dividends (interim ₹21, final ₹22), unclaimed dividend procedures, IEPF transfer rules, and historical unclaimed dividend data. It includes the AGM schedule, financial calendar, investor awareness and share transfer systems, investor conferences, grievance redressal, and share-related litigation. Share capital data covers ESOPs, category-wise and distribution shareholding, major shareholders, dematerialization status, listing codes, and credit ratings. It also covers shareholder communication, registered office, global locations, and subsidiaries.

nodes.title: Infosys ADS, Credit Ratings, Shareholder Communication, and Global Locations
key_items: Outstanding ADSs / GDRs / warrants or any convertible instruments
nodes.summary: The page covers Infosys's outstanding ADSs (traded on NYSE under 'INFY', each representing one equity share, with 130,339 record holders of 43,98,60,715 ADSs as of March 31, 2025, and no outstanding GDRs/warrants/convertible instruments); credit ratings from Moody's (Baa1 stable), S&P (A stable), Dun & Bradstreet (5A1 strong), and CRISIL (AAA stable) with no changes during the year; shareholder communication practices including website postings of quarterly reports, financial statements, earnings calls, AGM webcasts, Form 20-F, and other disclosures, as well as newspaper publications; and registered office address in Bengaluru, India, with operations across 292 locations in 59 countries (no manufacturing plants, but development centers and offices).

nodes.title: Subsidiaries
nodes.summary: The text details subsidiary information as of March 31, 2025, noting 30 direct and 76 step-down subsidiaries with no material subsidiary. It summarizes corporate governance regarding general body meetings, listing special resolutions from the 41st, 42nd, and 43rd AGMs, including dates, venues, resolutions, and webcast links. It states no extraordinary general meeting was held in fiscal 2025. It covers a postal ballot conducted in 2024 for related party transactions with Stater N.V. and Stater Nederland B.V., including voting results, approval date, scrutinizer details, and web link. It outlines the postal ballot procedure and confirms no special resolution is proposed for the ensuing AGM via postal ballot.

nodes.title: Legal compliance
nodes.summary: The text covers legal compliance, stating adherence to laws and disclosure of non-compliance details. It reports no penalties or non-compliance in the last three years, but mentions a Settlement order for the CEO. It includes CEO/CFO certification, adoption of a Code of Conduct with affirmed compliance, and a vigil/whistleblower mechanism with safeguards. Complaints on sexual harassment are referenced to the BRSR. Insider trading prevention includes amended codes effective April 2025. Discretionary requirements like separate Chairman/CEO roles and unmodified audit opinions are implemented. Other affirmations include compliance with Listing Regulations, no trading suspension, a certificate of non-disqualification of directors, and an auditors' certificate on corporate governance.

nodes.title: Annexure A: Certificate of non-disqualification of directors
nodes.summary: The text includes a certificate of non-disqualification of directors for Infosys Limited, certifying that none of the listed directors are debarred or disqualified by SEBI, MCA, or other authorities as of March 31, 2025. It lists the directors with their DINs and dates of appointment, and includes the auditor's signature and date. Additionally, it provides investor contact information for queries related to financial statements, shares, compliance, business responsibility, and sustainability, as well as details of the registrar and share transfer agents, depositary banks for ADS, custodians, and depositories for equity shares in India.

nodes.title: Investor contacts
nodes.summary: The text lists investor contacts at Infosys for financial statements, investor correspondence, share/dividend/compliance, business responsibility, and sustainability queries, plus registrar KFin Technologies and depositary banks Deutsche Bank and ICICI for ADS, and depositories NSDL and CDSL. It provides addresses of stock exchanges in India (NSE, BSE) and outside (NYSE). It then presents a risk management report by Deepak Bhalla, noting geopolitical, economic, supply chain, regulatory, technology, and cybersecurity risks. It describes Infosys' Enterprise Risk Management function, which identifies, analyzes, assesses, mitigates, monitors, and governs risks to achieve strategic objectives. The ERM framework covers emerging risks, strategy and execution, operational, and legal/compliance risks, using COSO and ISO 31000 best practices, with a four-point impact scale and risk categorization.

nodes.title: Risk management report
nodes.summary: The text covers Infosys' risk management report, detailing the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, its integration across three lines of defense, governance structure, and risk categories (strategic, operational, legal/compliance). It highlights key and emerging risks such as geopolitical, macroeconomic, technology disruption, talent constraints, cybersecurity, data privacy, ESG, contractual liabilities, and regulatory changes, along with mitigation strategies and impacted capitals. It also describes ERM features like risk analytics, process frameworks, risk culture, and fiscal 2025 initiatives. Additionally, it includes an independent assurance report on BRSR Core indicators, covering scope, criteria, management responsibilities, and inherent limitations.

nodes.title: BRSR Assurance Report
nodes.summary: The BRSR Assurance Report section features Deloitte's reasonable assurance report on Infosys's BRSR Core indicators for FY 2024-25, covering scope, SEBI criteria, responsibilities, limitations, independence, SSAE 3000/SAE 3410 standards, procedures, exclusions, other information, opinion, and use restrictions. Appendix I lists Principle-wise Essential Indicators (P-1, P-3, P-5, P-6, P-8, P-9) covering ethics, employee well-being, human rights, environment, inclusive growth, and consumer responsibility, with specifics like payables, concentration, well-being spending, safety, wages, harassment, energy, water, GHG, waste, sourcing, job creation, and data breaches. It also notes Infosys's sustainability commitment, ESG integration, GRI adoption, BRR publication, and alignment with NGRBC and SEBI Regulation 34(2)(f).

nodes.title: BRSR Assurance Report (intro)
nodes.summary: This independent practitioner's reasonable assurance report by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP for Infosys Limited covers the BRSR Core indicators in the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY ended March 31, 2025. It outlines the engagement scope, criteria based on SEBI regulations, management's responsibilities, inherent limitations, independence and quality control, the practitioner's responsibility under SSAE 3000 and SAE 3410, procedures performed, exclusions, other information, the reasonable assurance opinion, and restrictions on use. The report concludes that the BRSR Core indicators are prepared in all material respects in accordance with the criteria.

nodes.title: APPENDIX I
nodes.summary: Appendix I lists identified sustainability information subject to reasonable assurance, organized by BRSR Principle-wise Essential Indicators (P-1, P-3, P-5, P-6, P-8, P-9), covering ethics and transparency, employee well-being, human rights, environment, inclusive growth, and consumer responsibility. Specific indicators include accounts payables, purchase/sales concentration, employee well-being spending, safety incidents, female wages, sexual harassment complaints, energy, water, GHG emissions, waste, sustainable sourcing, job creation wages, and data breaches. The text also presents Infosys's sustainability commitment, ESG integration, GRI adoption (2008), early BRR publication (2013), and BRSR alignment with NGRBC principles and SEBI Regulation 34(2)(f).

nodes.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report
nodes.summary: The text is Infosys's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) for FY2024-25, covering corporate identity, ESG integration, and adherence to NGRBC principles. It details company information, business activities, employee data (including diversity and turnover), CSR, stakeholder engagement, and principle-wise performance on ethics, sustainability, human rights, environment, policy advocacy, inclusive growth, and consumer responsibility. It includes quantitative metrics on energy, water, emissions, waste, and health/safety, along with assurance statements, governance oversight, and a CEO/CFO certification.

nodes.title: CEO and CFO certification
nodes.summary: The CEO and CFO of Infosys Limited certify to the Board that they have reviewed the financial statements and Board's report for the year ended March 31, 2025. They confirm the statements are materially true, present a true and fair view, and comply with accounting standards and laws. They state no fraudulent or illegal transactions occurred except as disclosed. They affirm responsibility for disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting, including designing, evaluating, and disclosing changes and deficiencies. They disclose any significant changes in accounting policies and fraud instances to auditors and the Audit Committee. They affirm no denial of access to the Audit Committee and protection of whistleblowers. They declare all Board members and senior management complied with the Code of Conduct and Ethics.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statements
nodes.summary: The Standalone Financial Statements section for Infosys Limited for the year ended March 31, 2025, includes the Independent Auditor’s Report with annexures on internal financial controls and statutory compliance, and the audited financial statements: Balance Sheet, Statement of Profit and Loss, Statement of Changes in Equity, and Statement of Cash Flows. It also contains an overview and notes covering company background, basis of preparation, significant accounting policies, critical estimates, and detailed disclosures on assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses, employee benefits, taxes, financial instruments, related party transactions, CSR, segment reporting, and key ratios.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statements (intro)
nodes.summary: The text is an index for the Standalone Financial Statements under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) for the year ended March 31, 2025. It lists sections: Independent Auditor’s Report; Balance Sheet; Statement of Profit and Loss; Statement of Changes in Equity; Statement of Cash Flows; and Overview and Notes. The overview covers company overview, basis of preparation, use of estimates and judgments, and critical accounting estimates. The notes cover property, plant and equipment; goodwill and intangibles; leases; capital work-in-progress; investments; loans; other financial assets; trade receivables; cash and cash equivalents; other assets; financial instruments; equity; other financial liabilities; trade payables; other liabilities; provisions; income taxes; revenue from operations; other income; expenses; employee benefits; earnings per equity share; contingent liabilities and commitments; related party transactions; CSR; segment reporting; ratios; and function-wise classification of the Statement of Profit and Loss.

nodes.title: Independent Auditor’s Report
nodes.summary: This Independent Auditor’s Report covers the audit of Infosys Limited’s standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It includes the auditor’s opinion that the statements give a true and fair view under Indian Accounting Standards, with a basis for opinion emphasizing compliance and ethics. Key audit matters identified are revenue recognition involving judgment in performance obligations, principal vs. agent, and timing of fixed-price maintenance revenue, and revenue recognition for fixed-price contracts using percentage-of-completion requiring significant estimation; auditor responses and procedures are described. The report addresses other information, management’s and the Board’s responsibilities for preparation and internal controls, and the auditor’s responsibilities including risk assessment, internal financial controls, going concern, and communication with governance. It also covers reporting on legal and regulatory requirements under Section 143(3), director disqualifications, internal financial controls, remuneration compliance, Rule 11 matters, and the Companies (Auditor’s Report) Order, 2020.

nodes.title: Report on the Audit of the Standalone Financial Statements Opinion
nodes.summary: The Independent Auditor's Report for Infosys Limited's standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, presents the auditor's opinion that the financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with Indian Accounting Standards. It outlines the basis for opinion, emphasizing compliance with auditing standards and ethical requirements. The report identifies two key audit matters: revenue recognition involving judgment in identifying performance obligations, determining principal vs. agent, and timing of fixed-price maintenance revenue; and revenue recognition for fixed-price contracts using the percentage-of-completion method, which requires significant estimation. For each key audit matter, the auditor's response and procedures performed are described. The report also addresses other information, management's responsibilities, and the auditor's responsibilities.

nodes.title: Auditor and Management Responsibilities for Standalone Financial Statements
key_items: Information Other than the Financial Statements and Auditor’s Report Thereon
Responsibilities of Management and Board of Directors for the Standalone Financial Statements
nodes.summary: The page covers two sections from an auditor's report. The first section, 'Information Other than the Financial Statements and Auditor’s Report Thereon,' outlines the Board's responsibility for other information, the auditor's non-assurance opinion on it, and the auditor's responsibility to read and consider consistency, concluding no material misstatement was found. The second section details management's and the Board's responsibilities under section 134(5) of the Act for preparing standalone financial statements with a true and fair view, including maintaining accounting records, safeguarding assets, preventing fraud, selecting accounting policies, making judgments, designing internal controls, assessing going concern, and overseeing financial reporting.

nodes.title: Auditor’s Responsibilities for the Audit of the Standalone Financial Statements
nodes.summary: The auditor's objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance that the standalone financial statements are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue an opinion. The text explains that reasonable assurance is high but not a guarantee, defines material misstatements as those influencing economic decisions, and outlines the auditor's procedures: identifying and assessing risks, understanding internal financial controls (including expressing an opinion on their adequacy and effectiveness), evaluating accounting policies and estimates, concluding on going concern, and evaluating overall presentation. It discusses materiality in planning and evaluating misstatements, communicating with governance about scope, findings, independence, and key audit matters, and determining which matters to report as key audit matters.

nodes.title: Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
nodes.summary: The auditors report compliance with Section 143(3) of the Act: they obtained necessary information, found proper books of account, and confirmed the financial statements (Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss, Other Comprehensive Income, Changes in Equity, Cash Flows) agree with books and comply with Ind AS. They note no director disqualifications, reference an unmodified opinion on internal financial controls in Annexure A, confirm director remuneration complies with Section 197, and address Rule 11 matters: pending litigations disclosure, provisions for foreseeable losses, no long-term derivatives, timely transfer to Investor Education and Protection Fund, management representations on no undisclosed fund flows to/from ultimate beneficiaries, dividend compliance with Section 123, and accounting software with audit trail feature. They also reference Annexure B for Companies (Auditor’s Report) Order, 2020 matters.

nodes.title: Annexure “A” to the Independent Auditor’s Report
key_items: Management’s and Board of Directors’ Responsibilities for Internal Financial Controls
Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with reference to Standalone Financial Statements
nodes.summary: This annexure to the Independent Auditor's Report covers the audit of Infosys Limited's internal financial controls over standalone financial statements as of March 31, 2025. It outlines management's and the Board's responsibilities for establishing and maintaining these controls, based on ICAI criteria, and the auditor's responsibility to express an opinion based on their audit. The report defines internal financial controls, detailing policies and procedures for accurate records, authorized transactions, and asset safeguarding. It notes inherent limitations, such as potential management override. The auditors, Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP, conclude that the company maintained adequate and effectively operating internal financial controls in all material respects as of that date, based on the established criteria.

nodes.title: Annexure ‘B’ to the Independent Auditor’s Report
nodes.summary: This annexure to the Independent Auditor’s Report for Infosys Limited covers the auditor’s statements on: property, plant and equipment (PPE), right-of-use assets, and intangible assets—including record maintenance, physical verification, title deeds, no revaluation, and no benami proceedings; inventory (none) and working capital limits (none); investments and loans—details of loans to subsidiaries, compliance with Sections 185 and 186, and no guarantees; deposits (none); cost records (not applicable); statutory dues—regular deposits, no arrears, and disputed amounts with forums and amounts; no unrecorded income; borrowings (none), no wilful default, no term loans, and proper use of short-term funds; no public offer or preferential allotment; no fraud or ADT-4 filings, and consideration of whistleblower complaints; Nidhi Company (not applicable); compliance with Sections 177 and 188 for related party transactions; internal audit system adequacy; no non-cash transactions with directors; RBI registration (not required) and no core investment company; no cash losses; no statutory auditor resignation; no material uncertainty about going concern; and CSR compliance—no unspent amounts requiring transfer except ongoing projects where transfer to special account is pending due to time not elapsed.

nodes.title: Balance Sheet
nodes.summary: The text presents a balance sheet in ₹ crore for March 31, 2025, and 2024, detailing assets. It covers non-current assets including property, plant and equipment, right-of-use assets, capital work-in-progress, goodwill, financial assets (investments, loans, other financial assets), deferred tax assets, income tax assets, and other non-current assets, with total non-current assets. It then lists current assets: financial assets (investments, trade receivables, cash and cash equivalents, loans, other financial assets), income tax assets, and other current assets, with total current assets, total assets, and a page reference to Infosys Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Balance Sheet (contd.)
nodes.summary: This balance sheet excerpt presents equity and liabilities as of March 31, 2025, and 2024, with comparative figures. It details equity share capital and other equity, total equity, non-current liabilities including financial liabilities, lease liabilities, deferred tax liabilities, and other non-current liabilities, and current liabilities such as financial liabilities, lease liabilities, trade payables (split between micro/small enterprises and other creditors), other financial liabilities, other current liabilities, provisions, and income tax liabilities. It provides totals for non-current liabilities and current liabilities, concluding with total equity and liabilities. The document includes authentication signatures from Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP, Infosys Limited's Chairman, CFO, CEO/MD, Director, and Company Secretary, dated April 17, 2025, in Bengaluru, and references accompanying notes and the annual report.

nodes.title: Statement of Profit and Loss
nodes.summary: The text presents a Statement of Profit and Loss for the years ended March 31, 2025, and 2024, in ₹ crore (except per equity share data). It details revenue from operations, other income, total income, and various expenses including employee benefits, technical sub-contractors, travel, software, communication, consultancy, depreciation, finance cost, and other expenses, leading to total expenses and profit before tax. It further breaks down tax expense into current and deferred tax, resulting in profit for the year. Notes for certain line items are referenced, and the document is identified as part of the Infosys Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Statement of Profit and Loss (contd.)
nodes.summary: This text presents continued financial statements from Infosys' Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, covering the Statement of Profit and Loss, Statement of Changes in Equity, and related notes. It details other comprehensive income items, including remeasurement of defined benefit plans and fair value changes on derivatives and investments, along with total comprehensive income, earnings per share (basic and diluted), and weighted average shares. The Statement of Changes in Equity shows movements in share capital, reserves (capital redemption, securities premium, special economic zone reinvestment, etc.), retained earnings, and other equity for years ended March 31, 2024 and 2025, including profit, dividends, stock option transactions, and transfers. It includes auditor signatures and board approvals.

nodes.title: Statement of Cash Flows
nodes.summary: The text presents the Statement of Cash Flows for Infosys Limited for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, using the indirect method. It begins with an accounting policy explaining the segregation of cash flows into operating, investing, and financing activities, and the treatment of cash equivalents. Detailed line items show cash flows from operating activities, including profit adjustments, changes in assets and liabilities, and income taxes paid. Investing activities cover capital expenditures, deposits, loans, investments, and proceeds from sales. Financing activities include lease payments, stock option proceeds, dividends, and other payments. The statement concludes with the net increase/decrease in cash, exchange differences, opening and closing cash balances, and supplementary information on restricted cash. Signatures from auditors and directors are also included.

nodes.title: Overview and Notes to the Standalone Financial Statements
nodes.summary: This text comprises the standalone financial statements of Infosys Limited for FY2024-25, including an overview of the company and basis of preparation; significant accounting policies and critical estimates; detailed notes on property, plant and equipment, goodwill, intangible assets, leases, capital work-in-progress, investments, loans, other financial assets, trade receivables, cash, other assets, financial instruments (including fair value hierarchy and risk management), equity, share-based payments, other financial liabilities, trade payables, provisions, income taxes, revenue recognition, other income, expenses, employee benefits (gratuity, pension, provident fund, superannuation, compensated absences), earnings per share, contingent liabilities, related party transactions, CSR, segment reporting, key ratios, and function-wise classification of the Statement of Profit and Loss.

nodes.title: Consolidated Financial Statements

nodes.title: Independent Auditor’s Report
nodes.summary: This Independent Auditor's Report for Infosys Limited's consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, presents an unmodified opinion that the statements give a true and fair view in accordance with Ind AS. nodes.title: Annexure “A” To The Independent Auditor’s Report
nodes.summary: This annexure to the Independent Auditor's Report covers the audit of internal financial controls (IFC) over consolidated financial statements of Infosys Limited and its Indian subsidiaries as of March 31, 2025. It outlines management's and the Board's responsibilities for establishing and maintaining IFC based on ICAI criteria, and the auditor's responsibility to express an opinion based on audit procedures. It defines IFC, discusses inherent limitations, and concludes with the auditor's opinion that the company and its subsidiaries have adequate and effectively operating IFC in all material respects. The report is signed by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP.

nodes.title: Financial risk management Financial risk factors (intro)
nodes.summary:
Financial risk management Financial risk factors
The Group's activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: market risk, credit risk and liquidity risk. The Group's primary focus is to foresee the unpredictability of financial markets and seek to minimize potential adverse effects on its financial performance. The primary market risk to the Group is foreign exchange risk. The Group uses derivative financial instruments to mitigate foreign exchange related risk exposures. The Group's exposure to credit risk is influenced mainly by the individual characteristic of each customer and the concentration of risk from the top few customers.

nodes.title: Foreign currency Accounting policy
nodes.summary: The text outlines Infosys's foreign currency accounting policy, including functional currency determination (Indian rupee for parent/Indian subsidiaries, local currencies for foreign subsidiaries) and financial statement presentation in Indian rupees. It details translation of foreign-currency transactions: monetary assets/liabilities at balance sheet rates with gains/losses in profit or loss unless qualifying cash flow hedges deferred in OCI; non-monetary items at fair value or historical cost rates; revenue/expenses at transaction-date rates; settlement gains/losses in net profit. Foreign subsidiary financial statement translation uses balance sheet rates for assets/liabilities and average rates for revenue/expenses/cash flows, with gains/losses in currency translation reserves under equity, transferred to net profit on full disposal, and equity-recorded for ownership changes without control loss. OCI includes translation differences on non-monetary FVOCI assets. Goodwill and fair value adjustments on foreign acquisitions are translated at balance sheet rates. Government grant policy recognizes grants with reasonable assurance, treating asset-related grants as deferred income over useful life and revenue-related grants systematically to match costs. nodes.title: Instructions for e-voting
nodes.summary: This section provides comprehensive e-voting instructions for shareholders, covering login methods for individual demat shareholders via NSDL, CDSL, or depository participants, as well as for other shareholders and physical mode holders, including password recovery and helpdesk contacts. It details User ID formats and password procedures for non-individual shareholders, followed by step-by-step e-voting process from login to vote confirmation. General guidelines address institutional shareholder requirements, password security, grievance contacts, and processes for shareholders without registered email IDs. Key AGM information includes date, mode, helpline, record date, dividend details, and e-voting schedule. A safe harbor statement outlines forward-looking statements, risks, and legal notices.

nodes.title: (A) Login method for e-voting for individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode
key_items: Type of shareholders; Login Method; Login type; Helpdesk details
nodes.summary: The text provides detailed instructions for electronic voting on the NSDL e-voting system. It outlines two main steps, focusing on Step 1: Access. It details login methods for individual shareholders in demat mode with NSDL (via IDeAS or OTP) and CDSL (via Easi/Easiest or direct OTP), and through depository participants. For other shareholders and those in physical mode, it explains login via the NSDL e-voting website or IDeAS. It includes important notes on password recovery and provides helpdesk contact information for NSDL and CDSL technical issues.

nodes.title: Your User ID is:
nodes.summary: The text outlines User ID formats for shareholding modes: NSDL (8-character DP ID + 8-digit Client ID), CDSL (16-digit Beneficiary ID), and physical (EVEN + Folio Number). It provides password details for non-individual shareholders, including using existing passwords, retrieving initial passwords via email attachment (password is Client ID or Folio Number), and recovery steps for forgotten passwords via website options, email request, or OTP login. It then details the e-voting process: login by entering password, agreeing to terms, clicking login, selecting the company's EVEN, casting vote by choosing assent/dissent, verifying shares, submitting and confirming, with a success message and print option, and notes that confirmed votes cannot be modified.

nodes.title: General guidelines for shareholders
nodes.summary: The text provides guidelines for shareholders regarding e-voting, covering institutional shareholders' requirement to submit board resolutions and authority letters via email or upload, password security and reset procedures after failed attempts, and contact details for queries and grievances. It also outlines the process for shareholders without registered email IDs to obtain user IDs and passwords, detailing document submission for physical and demat holdings, an alternative request method, and SEBI circular compliance allowing demat holders to vote through depository participants, emphasizing the need to update mobile and email in demat accounts.
